notes.text: The explanation paraphrases the 'Best practices for exceptions' page as saying callers should be able to assume no side effects when an exception is thrown (section on restoring state when methods do not complete, with a money-transfer example). I believe this section exists, but its exact wording should be checked against the page.
The term 'strong exception guarantee' comes from the C++ exception-safety literature (Abrahams). It is not necessarily used verbatim on Microsoft Learn; it is used here as a general concept.

The second link (design-guidelines/exception-throwing) gives general guidance on throwing exceptions and only indirectly supports the state-consistency claim. Consider replacing it if the fact-checker finds a better source.

bugLineSets accepts [17] and [17, 18]. Line 18 alone is not accepted, because the check itself is correct and only its position after the debit is wrong. Snippet output traced by hand: 'Transfer failed: Account B is frozen' / 'Total: 120'. The fixed version prints 'Total: 150'. Run-snippets confirmation is still needed.
